subject: Business Models
title: Nintendo: Cards to Consoles
description: A micro-lesson that makes Nintendo: Cards to Consoles usable.

hook.text: Nintendo was founded in 1889 as a playing card company. It took 88 years to make its first video game.

buildup.text: Between cards and games, Nintendo tried taxis, love hotels, and instant rice. All failed.

discovery.text: In 1977, Nintendo released its first home console. The NES arrived in 1985 and resurrected the gaming industry.

twist.text: Nintendo doesn't compete on specs. The Wii and Switch used inferior hardware with innovative gameplay concepts.

climax.text: Nintendo's model: sell affordable hardware with must-have first-party games. The ecosystem is the moat.

punchline.text: Playing cards in 1889, Switch in 2017. 128 years of business model reinvention.

quiz.question: What was Nintendo's original product when founded in 1889?

details.summary: Nintendo has reinvented its business model repeatedly since 1889, from playing cards to toys to video game consoles to mobile gaming. Each transition responded to market limits while leveraging existing capabilities in entertainment, design, and creativity.
details.whyItMatters: Nintendo's 135-year survival through multiple model transitions shows that longevity requires willingness to reinvent fundamentally. Its focus on creative play over technical specifications is a masterclass in differentiation-based strategy.
takeaways: Nintendo pivoted from playing cards to toys to consoles over 135 years
The company prioritizes creative gameplay over raw technical power
Hardware innovation like the Wii and Switch created new market categories

faq.question: How has Nintendo survived while competitors failed?
faq.answer: Nintendo focuses on unique gameplay experiences rather than competing on hardware specs. The Wii attracted non-gamers with motion controls. The Switch combined portable and home gaming. This blue ocean strategy avoids direct competition with PlayStation and Xbox.

faq.question: What are the key phases of Nintendo's business model evolution?
faq.answer: Playing cards from 1889, various toy products in the 1960s and 70s, arcade games in the early 1980s, home consoles from 1983 with the NES, handheld gaming with Game Boy, motion gaming with Wii, hybrid portable-home gaming with Switch.
